thread:
support_jen: Hey team — customer ACME-Analytics says their Dedicated pool (pool-az-3) had 720 reserved GPU hours this billing month but the invoice line shows 852 GPU-hours billed. Dashboard token usage looks normal (~1.2B tokens). They insist they didn't use burst beyond policy. Can someone triage?

billing_jen: Can you paste the invoice line and pool id? I can pull meter events.

support_jen: Invoice snippet:```
Invoice LineItem: reserved_pool_hours: pool-az-3; quantity: 852; unit_price: 2.50
Customer dashboard (UI): reserved_hours_used: 720
Token usage: ~1.2B tokens (matches their app logs)
```

ajay: Quick hypothesis: metering counts any GPU attach time (including orchestrator maintenance / model prefetch) against reserved hours, but token-metering only records per-request tokens. If there's a background job that keeps nodes warmed or does KV checkpointing, it can burn GPU-hours with zero tokens. Any recent maintenance or autoscaler activity?

ops_ron: We had a scheduled KV compaction job in pool-az-3 on 2026-02-12 03:00 UTC that spun up workers for ~28 hours because of a stuck pod. That would count as GPU-hours. I can share logs.

support_jen: That could explain ~28 hours but not the whole delta (~132 hours). The customer says they didn't see unexpected latency or errors during that window.

ajay: Can we correlate the billing meter events with node attach/detach and with "batcher"/"prefetch" processes? Use internal metering endpoint:```
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" "https://internal-metrics.redwood/pools/pool-az-3/metering?from=2026-02-01&to=2026-02-28" | jq .events | less
```

metering-bot: Metering dump queued. Generating per-event breakdown (this can take ~30s).

billing_jen: Pulled events. There's a pattern: many small "attach" events with reason=maintenance and reason=warmup between 00:00-06:00 UTC across multiple days, and a cluster of continuous attaches on 2026-02-18 because of a failed autoscaler loop. I can export csv.

ops_ron: The failed autoscaler loop created and recreated 6 pods repeatedly for ~52 hours; each create attached a GPU and leaked a short-lived container that never recorded token usage. That aligns with the missing hours. Root cause: a race in our scale-down probe when a node had an older runtime image.

maria_cs: For the customer-facing side: can we quantify hours attributable to maintenance/leak vs actual request-driven usage? We need a concise explanation and propose credits if warranted.

ajay: Yes. From meter events I see ~128 GPU-hours where token_count==0 and reason in ["maintenance","warmup","autoscaler-recreate"]. Another ~4 hours for KV checkpoint jobs. Total ~132 hours, which explains the invoice vs dashboard delta.

billing_jen: Proposed customer remedy: (1) apply a one-time invoice credit for 132 GPU-hours at their reserved rate; (2) mark those meter events as internal and exclude from future token-based dashboards; (3) add a note on the invoice explanation. Approve?

maria_cs: Approve. Please prepare a short customer message: say we traced the discrepancy to orchestration maintenance and an autoscaler loop that created short-lived GPU attachments which are billed as reserved hours but do not generate token counts. Offer credit and outline mitigation steps.

ops_ron: Mitigation steps: patch scale-down probe (PR #4478), add a guard to prevent double-create in autoscaler, and add an internal flag so meter events with reason starting with "internal-" are excluded from customer-facing dashboards. I'll target a hotfix deploy today.

support_jen: Drafting customer reply now. Will say: "We traced the discrepancy to internal maintenance and an autoscaler bug that created short-lived GPU attachments without token usage. We've credited 132 GPU-hours to your account and deployed a patch to prevent recurrence."

billing_jen: Done — applied credit and updated invoice note. Ticket #INC-2026-1198

maria_cs: Thanks all. I'll send the customer the summary and next steps. Please drop the meter CSV in the ticket for audit. :thumbsup:

support_jen: Uploading CSV and attach logs to INC-2026-1198 now.

metering-bot: CSV and event ids attached to INC-2026-1198.
